q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
note: The symbol comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

q: What is the chemical formula for water?
note: The molecule is bent rather than straight, and that lopsided shape is what makes water such a good solvent.

q: Which metal has the chemical symbol Fe?
note: It comes from ferrum, the Latin name, which also gives us words like ferrous and farrier.

q: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance on Earth?
note: It is pure carbon, the same element as the soft graphite in a pencil, just packed together differently.

q: What is the chemical name for ordinary table salt?
note: In mineral form it is called halite, making it more or less the only rock that people routinely eat.

q: Which element is first on the periodic table and the lightest of them all?
note: It is also by far the most abundant element in the universe.

q: Which metal has the chemical symbol Pb?
note: It comes from the Latin plumbum, which is also the root of the word plumber.

q: Which is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature?
note: It was long known as quicksilver, and it is so dense that an iron ball will float on it.

q: What does the pH scale measure?
a: How acidic or alkaline something is
note: Seven is neutral, lower is acidic and higher is alkaline, and every single step is a tenfold change.

q: Which gas, the second lightest of all, is used to make party balloons float?
note: It was spotted in the light of the Sun in 1868, years before anyone managed to find any on Earth.

q: Which acid does the human stomach produce to help digest food?
note: It is strong enough to attack metal, so the stomach lining constantly renews itself to cope.

q: What is the term for a solid turning straight into a gas without becoming a liquid first?
note: Dry ice does exactly this at everyday temperatures, which is why it makes fog instead of a puddle.

q: What is the name for a substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up itself?
note: The catalytic converter in a car uses precious metals this way to clean up exhaust gases.

q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
note: Copper is used for wiring instead purely because it is so much cheaper.

q: In the periodic table, what does an element's atomic number tell you?
a: The number of protons in its nucleus
note: Change the number of protons and you have changed the element itself, which is why they are ordered this way.

q: Which metal is extracted from the ore bauxite?
note: It was once more precious than gold, until cheap electricity made smelting it straightforward.

q: Which metal, prized for its extremely high melting point, has the chemical symbol W?
note: The symbol comes from its other name, wolfram, and it melts at a higher temperature than any other metal.

q: What name is given to the group of very unreactive gases in the far-right column of the periodic table?
note: Their outer electron shells are already full, so they have almost no interest in bonding with anything.

q: Which acid gives vinegar its sour taste and sharp smell?
note: Ordinary vinegar is only about five percent acetic acid, with the rest being mostly water.

q: Stainless steel is iron and carbon mixed with which other element to stop it rusting?
note: The chromium forms an invisible oxide layer that seals the surface and reforms whenever it is scratched.
